globals.meaning: The root command entry (path=[]) is the canonical location for opencode's global flags. opencode repeats its global flags in every subcommand's help output, so without this model the union records one copy per subcommand and the coverage report counts each copy as a distinct missing surface.

effective_flags_model.definition: A command's effective flag set is the union of root flags and that command's own flags.
effective_flags_model.reporting: Coverage deltas for global flags are reported only under the root path ([]).

union_normalization.meaning: If a command help listing repeats a global flag already present in root flags (same canonical key), omit it from that command's flags in the union snapshot. The flag remains globally available via the effective_flags_model.

notes: The model is declared and disabled, deliberately. It is incompatible with this descriptor's parity exclusions, which remove the root command and all 20 of its flags because the root command starts the interactive TUI. The model relocates a global flag's coverage reporting to the root path; those root entries are parity-excluded; so an enabled model reports the surface nowhere at all. See uaa-0052.

Measured against opencode 1.18.30 on 2026-09-21, rebuilding the pinned packet with the model on and off: missing_flags 394 -> 49, and excluded_flags stayed at 20 both ways. All 345 removed rows were subcommand copies of the 20 parity-excluded root keys, and they appeared under no delta list at all - not missing, not excluded. Each of those 20 exclusion units carries the note 'where a subcommand accepts the same flag, that copy stays in parity', which is the policy the dedupe inverts.

The 345 repeated rows are real work items, not noise, because opencode's wrapper covers one command. Suppressing them is a coverage decision that belongs in parity_exclusions, where an excluded unit keeps a visible excluded_* row with a category and a reason, and not in a structural switch that leaves no record. Doing that per unit is 345 hand-written entries today, so the enabling change is an exclusion form that can cover a path pattern. Until that exists, the honest number stands.
positional_args_model is deliberately not declared. opencode's only root positional arg (project) is parity-excluded as interactive, and no consumer deserializes the key.

notes: This block declares the one field a consumer reads: manifest_acquisition.rs resolves allow_promote_when_incomplete and .github/workflows/parity-promote.yml gates on the resolved value. It states explicitly the stance opencode previously held by omitting the key, and changes no behaviour.

opencode does not adopt codex's mode/requirements_for_latest_validated_and_current keys: nothing deserializes them, so declaring them here would document promotion behaviour this descriptor does not control.

filter_semantics.any: Surface is considered present if it appears on at least one available input target.
filter_semantics.all: Surface is considered present only if it appears on all expected_targets.
filter_semantics.exact_target: Surface is considered present only if it appears on the specified target_triple.

wrapper_only_policy.meaning: Wrapper coverage entries with no corresponding upstream surface (after platform filtering). Treat as stale or wrapper-only and surface for cleanup/review.

statuses.snapshotted: Snapshots generated and schema-valid; no wrapper claims.
statuses.reported: Coverage report generated; work queue available; no wrapper validation claim.
statuses.supported: Wrapper coverage meets the support-matrix policy requirements for this version (stronger than validated).

notes: supported means there are no uncovered (missing/unknown/unsupported) upstream surfaces on any expected target under the support-matrix contract; every surfaced command/flag/arg is either supported (explicit/passthrough) or explicitly waived (intentionally_unsupported with rationale).
supported is a documentation/policy guarantee derived from coverage mapping; it does not replace real-binary validation (validated) for promotion.

validation_contract.meaning: versions/<v>.json.validation.{passed_targets,failed_targets,skipped_targets} must be disjoint subsets of expected_targets, and the required target must appear in exactly one of the sets (never implicit).

notes: Automation must only push commits to the dedicated PR branch for the target upstream version.
Human approval gates can be applied at merge time or via a separate staging branch.
CI must fail if any committed artifact does not validate against SCHEMA.json.
Raw help artifacts are not committed and are not schema-validated.
To avoid churn in committed artifacts, CI should set collected_at deterministically (e.g., from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH).
Prefer omitting report timestamps from committed reports; if present, make them deterministic in CI.
updated_at should be deterministic in CI to keep diffs stable across reruns.

uniqueness_scope.note: Collisions across different command paths are expected and allowed; uniqueness is enforced only within a single command scope.
